nodes.name: CuMo-BTC Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 900 mg of 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid (BTC) was dissolved in ethanol (40 mL), and 90 mg of L-glutamic acid, 182 mg of cupric acetate monohydrate, and 300 mg of molybdatophosphoric acid hydrate were dissolved in deionized water (40 mL). Then, the solution of BTC was slowly and regularly added to the deionized water solution with a syringe under agitation and stirring. The mixture was stirred for 12 h. The resulting white sample was collected by centrifugation, washed three times with ethanol, and then dried in a vacuum oven at room temperature for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: First, 900 mg of 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid (BTC) was dissolved in ethanol (40 mL)... dried in a vacuum oven at room temperature for 12 h.

nodes.name: Cu-BTC Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthesis method of Cu-BTC was the same as CuMo-BTC except for the addition of molybdatophosphoric acid hydrate.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis method of Cu-BTC was the same as above except for the addition of molybdatophosphoric acid hydrate.

nodes.name: CuMo/C Annealing
nodes.procedure: CuMo-BTC was heated to 800°C at a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ and kept at 800°C for 4 h in a 2:98 H₂/Ar furnace to obtain CuMo/C.

nodes.name: PdCu-MoOx Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The 20 mg of as-prepared CuMo/C was dispersed in 10 mL of ethanol under agitated stirring and sonicated to obtain a homogeneous mixed solution, followed by the addition of 2 mL of PdCl₂ solution (0.01 g mL⁻¹). Then, after reacting at a temperature of 40°C for 2 h, the sample was collected by centrifugation immediately and dried in a vacuum oven at 50°C for 12 h to obtain the PdCu-MoOx electrocatalyst.

nodes.name: PdCu Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The 20 mg as-prepared Cu/C was dispersed in 10 mL of ethanol under agitated stirring and sonicated to obtain a homogeneous mixed solution, followed by the addition of 1.4 mL of PdCl₂ solution (0.01 g mL⁻¹). Then, after reacting at a temperature of 80°C for 2 h, the sample was collected by centrifugation immediately and dried in a vacuum oven at 50°C for 12 h to obtain the PdCu electrocatalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: PdCu-MoOx shows diffraction peaks similar to Pd with systematic shift to higher 2θ angles indicating PdCu alloy formation; no crystalline Mo-based phases detected despite ICP-OES showing Mo presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PXRD measurements revealed that the PdCu-MoOx samples presented a similar diffraction peak as Pd (ICDD PDF No. 46-1043) (Figure S6a) and have a systematic peak shift to higher 2θ angles, indicating the formation of a PdCu alloy... despite the findings of the Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrum (ICP-OES) (Table S1) suggesting the presence of Mo, there are no crystalline phases of Mo-based species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad and diffuse molecular spectral bands conclusively demonstrate existence of amorphous MoOx species within the PdCu-MoOx catalyst system.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on this, Raman spectroscopy was completed to characterize the structure. The broad and diffuse nature of these molecular spectral bands conclusively demonstrates the existence of amorphous MoOx species within the catalyst system (Figure S6b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aggregates consist of nanoparticles with average diameters 6-7 nm; interplanar spacings of 0.192 nm and 0.220 nm correlate with (111) and (200) facets of PdCu alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figures 1a and S7, the aggregates consist of many nanoparticles with average diameters ranging from 6 to 7 nm. The interplanar spacings of 0.192 and 0.220 nm in Figure 1a-c strongly correlate with the (111) and (200) facets of the PdCu alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: ACHAADF-STEM images show amorphous compound regions enriched with Mo and O surrounding PdCu nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To obtain more detailed information, images of ACHAADF-STEM with increased magnification were obtained and are presented in Figures 1d,e, S8, and S9. The EDS results demonstrate that the amorphous compound region is enriched with Mo and O, while Pd and Cu are absent.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Pd and Cu in nanoparticles; Mo consistently present in regions where Cu and Pd are less abundant; amorphous regions surrounding nanoparticles enriched with Mo and O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Figure 1f-i, and Figure S8) revealed a uniform distribution of Pd and Cu in the nanoparticles. Instead, Mo is consistently present in regions in which Cu and Pd are less abundant.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd 3d spectrum of PdCu-MoOx shifts to lower binding energy vs Pd/C indicating electron flow to Pd; Mo 3d binding energy between MoO3 and MoO2 with 29.84% Mo5+ and average oxidation state +5.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with commercial Pd/C, the Pd 3d XPS spectrum of PdCu-MoOx shifts to a lower binding energy, suggesting that more electrons flow to Pd (Figure 2a)... 29.84% of the surface Mo5+ exists in PdCu-MoOx, and the average oxidation state of Mo is +5.5.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Mo K-edge XANES spectra show absorption edge position of PdCu-MoOx between MoO2 and MoO3 but nearer to MoO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized Mo K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 2c) show that the position of the absorption edge of PdCu-MoOx is also between those of MoO2 and MoO3 but nearer to that of MoO3, thereby corroborating the XPS findings.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra show distal Mo-Mo coordination peak (~3Å) decreases and becomes almost negligible in PdCu-MoOx compared to MoO3; Mo-O bond length 1.78 Å slightly larger than in MoO3 and MoO2, indicating O-vacancy defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In PdCu-MoOx, the distal Mo-Mo coordination (~3Å) peak decreases compared to MoO3, which becomes almost negligible. Moreover, the bond length of Mo-O (1.78 Å) in PdCu-MoOx is slightly larger than that in MoO3 and MoO2, indicating a different Mo-O coordination environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms presence of Mo in PdCu-MoOx (Table S1).
